title: How Many Inactive Wells Remain? | CAPIT Data Context
description: Understanding inactive, orphaned, and idle well counts across state and federal inventories.
headline: How Many Inactive Wells Remain?
body: Counts vary widely depending on the source agency, regulatory definitions, and publication dates. CAPIT provides full transparency into whether a figure refers to unplugged orphaned wells, broader inactive-well estimates, or state-specific inventories.

sections.heading: Orphaned vs. Inactive Wells
sections.body: An orphaned well is a well with no solvent operator legally responsible for its plugging and site restoration. An inactive or idle well is simply a well that is not currently producing, but may still have a solvent operator on record.
bullets: Orphaned Wells: High priority for state and federal plugging programs (e.g., IIJA grants).
Inactive / Idle Wells: Tracked by state regulatory commissions with varying compliance deadlines.
Plugged Wells: Officially sealed and verified in state public registries.

sections.heading: State and Federal Inventories
sections.body: Different agencies report counts on different schedules. CAPIT continuously normalizes data from sources like the Railroad Commission of Texas (RRC), Pennsylvania DEP, and Oklahoma Corporation Commission (OCC) to maintain an accurate national snapshot.
